questions.topic: Safety in Auto Parts Merchandising Shop
questions.stem: A storekeeper is lifting cartons of brake drums from a high shelf. Which safety item protects his toes if a drum slips?
questions.explanation: Safety boots with steel toe caps protect the feet from falling heavy parts.

questions.stem: A mechanic brings an old part to the shop: a forged rod with a small eye at one end for the gudgeon pin and a split big end at the other. The part is the
questions.explanation: The connecting rod joins the piston (small end, gudgeon pin) to the crankshaft (split big end).

questions.stem: A customer complains that his clutch slips and smells of burning. Which part is he MOST likely to need?
questions.explanation: A worn friction lining on the clutch plate causes slip and burning smell.

questions.stem: A gearbox that changes ratios by itself using a torque converter and planetary gears is
questions.explanation: Automatic transmissions select ratios without a clutch pedal, using a torque converter and epicyclic gear sets.

questions.topic: Transmission System (Propeller Shaft and Rear Axle Assembly)
questions.stem: The cross-shaped part with four needle-roller cups that allows a propeller shaft to drive through an angle is the
questions.explanation: A Hooke-type universal joint uses a spider (cross) and needle-roller bearing cups.

questions.stem: A heavy lorry rear axle is usually carried on
options: a torsion bar in the steering column
questions.explanation: Multi-leaf springs carry heavy loads and also locate the beam axle.

questions.stem: The part that drives the water pump and fan on many older engines is the
questions.explanation: A V-belt from the crankshaft pulley drives the water pump and fan (and often the alternator).

questions.stem: A customer with power-assisted steering complains that the steering has suddenly become very heavy. Which item should the seller suggest he checks first?
options: The pump belt and fluid level
questions.explanation: Loss of assistance is usually from a slipping/broken pump belt or low fluid.

questions.stem: In a disc brake, the friction material is fitted to the
questions.explanation: Disc brakes use pads clamped by a caliper; shoes are used in drum brakes.

questions.stem: Wheel bearings and chassis joints are usually lubricated with grease rather than oil because grease
options: is thinner and flows faster to every part
stays in place and seals out dirt
can be poured into the sump
questions.explanation: Grease is semi-solid, so it stays where it is put and helps exclude water and dirt.

questions.stem: A fuse in a vehicle circuit is there to
options: store charge for the starter motor when cranking
step up voltage for the plugs
questions.explanation: The fuse protects wiring and components by melting on overload.

questions.stem: A customer with wire spoke wheels on an old motor car asks for tyres. The seller should supply
options: tubed tyres, because spoke rims are not airtight
tubeless tyres, because they suit every rim
any tyre of a smaller rim diameter
questions.explanation: Spoke nipples pass through the rim well, so the rim cannot hold air and an inner tube is needed.

questions.topic: Types of Tools and Their Uses
questions.stem: Which of these is a GENERAL tool found in every auto parts shop?
questions.explanation: Spanners are general tools; pullers, extractors and compressors are special tools for particular jobs.

questions.stem: After use, sockets and spanners should be wiped, lightly oiled and kept in a tool box mainly to
questions.explanation: Cleaning and light oiling prevent corrosion; boxes keep tools organised so none are lost.

questions.stem: The tester used to measure how long the contact breaker points stay closed is the
questions.explanation: Dwell is the angle during which points are closed; a dwell meter measures it.

questions.stem: The BEST source of information on how to start, use and maintain a new engine analyser is the
questions.explanation: The manufacturer's manual gives the correct operation and care procedure.

questions.stem: Which of these is an accessory?
questions.explanation: Accessories add comfort or appearance and are not needed for the vehicle to run.

questions.stem: Rubber parts such as wiper blades and hoses should be stored
options: on the roof of the shop where there is space
in a heap on the floor
questions.explanation: Heat, sunlight and petrol make rubber crack and perish.

questions.stem: A catalogue helps a parts seller mainly to
options: find the correct part number for a vehicle
questions.explanation: Catalogues list parts with numbers, illustrations and vehicle applications so the right part can be identified.

questions.stem: A shop uses at most 15 sets of brake pads a day and its supplier takes at most 6 days to deliver. The re-order level is
questions.explanation: Re-order level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 15 x 6 = 90.

questions.stem: A dealer bought 40 bulbs at ₦500 each, then 60 at ₦650 each, and sold 70. Using FIFO, the value of the bulbs left in stock is
questions.explanation: FIFO issues the oldest first: 40 at ₦500 and 30 at ₦650 are sold, leaving 30 x ₦650 = ₦19,500.

questions.stem: Using the same figures under LIFO, the value of the remaining 30 bulbs is
questions.explanation: LIFO issues the latest first: 60 at ₦650 and 10 at ₦500 are sold, leaving 30 x ₦500 = ₦15,000.

questions.stem: An advantage of arranging parts neatly by vehicle make and model on open display is that
options: customers and staff locate parts quickly
questions.explanation: Good visual presentation saves time and attracts buyers.

questions.stem: Counting and recording all the parts in a shop at the end of each year is
questions.explanation: An annual (yearly) stock-take is an inventory carried out once a year.

questions.stem: Buying genuine parts directly from the manufacturer's authorised distributor helps a dealer to
options: avoid fake parts and keep customers' trust
questions.explanation: Reliable sources give genuine, traceable parts and protect the shop's reputation.

questions.stem: Displaying parts at a stand in a trade fair in Lagos is a method of
questions.explanation: Trade fairs are one of the selling methods, along with shops, door-to-door and personal selling.

questions.stem: A dealer invoices 6 radiator hoses at ₦3,200 each less 5% trade discount. The invoice total is
Forecasting helps an auto parts business mainly to
options: repair faulty parts returned by customers
fix vehicle prices for the government
questions.explanation: Forecasting estimates future demand so that stock, staff and funds can be planned.

questions.stem: The book of original entry in which credit purchases of parts from suppliers are first recorded is the
questions.explanation: Credit purchases are entered first in the purchases journal (day book).

questions.stem: Money that the owner takes from personal savings to open a shop is an example of
questions.explanation: Personal savings are an internal (owner's) source of finance.

questions.stem: Grouping customers by where they live, such as Onitsha, Nnewi and Awka, is segmentation by
questions.explanation: Geographic segmentation divides a market according to location.

questions.stem: A dealer buys an alternator for ₦20,000 and sells it for ₦26,000. The profit as a percentage of the SELLING price (margin) is about
questions.explanation: Margin = 6,000/26,000 x 100 = 23.1%; 30% is the mark-up on cost.

questions.stem: Which of these is an advertising medium?
questions.explanation: Radio is a broadcast medium for advertising.

questions.stem: Allowing a mechanic to return an unused, unopened part within seven days for a refund is a form of
questions.explanation: Return and refund policies are part of good customer service.

questions.stem: To claim a warranty on a battery that failed after three months, the customer should normally present
options: the receipt and the warranty card
questions.explanation: Proof of purchase and the warranty document are required for a claim.

questions.stem: The Nigerian body that checks that imported auto parts meet approved standards is the
questions.explanation: SON sets and enforces standards for products, including auto parts.

questions.stem: Auto parts merchandising involves
options: buying, stocking, displaying and selling vehicle parts
questions.explanation: Merchandising covers the activities that get parts to buyers profitably.

questions.stem: A parts seller who can quickly identify a part from its shape and number shows good
questions.explanation: Product knowledge lets the seller supply the right part and advise customers.

questions.stem: Mr Eze is praised by mechanics in Nnewi for his honesty. Which practice is MOST likely to have earned him this praise?
options: Repainting old parts and selling them as new
Changing part numbers to raise prices
Selling fake parts at genuine prices
Telling a customer that a part is used or reconditioned
questions.explanation: Honest disclosure is ethical; the others deceive or exploit customers.

questions.stem: A shop sold 120, 150 and 135 batteries in the last three months. Using a simple three-month moving average, the forecast for next month is

(a) Name five parts of an engine lubrication system and state the function of each. [10 marks]
(b) Distinguish between oil and grease. [4 marks]
(c) A customer asks for oil for an old engine and for a modern car in a hot climate. Explain how SAE 40 and SAE 20W-50 differ and which you would recommend for each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) sump: stores oil
2 marks: (a) oil pump: circulates oil under pressure
2 marks: (a) oil filter: removes dirt from oil
2 marks: (a) oil pressure switch: operates warning light when pressure is low
2 marks: (a) oil cooler/oil seal: cools oil / prevents leakage (any one)
2 marks: (b) oil is liquid, flows to parts and carries heat away
2 marks: (b) grease is semi-solid, stays in place, used in bearings and joints
2 marks: (c) SAE 40 is single grade with fixed viscosity rating at operating temperature
2 marks: (c) 20W-50 is multigrade: thin when cold (20W) and as thick as SAE 50 when hot
2 marks: (c) recommendation: SAE 40 suitable for the old engine (as maker specified); 20W-50 for modern car in hot climate
questions.explanation: Lubrication parts: sump stores, pump circulates, filter cleans, pressure switch warns, cooler/seal. Oil flows and cools; grease stays in place. SAE 40 is single grade; 20W-50 multigrade flows cold yet stays thick hot.

questions.stem:
(a) State the function of each of the following: battery, alternator, ignition coil, electronic control unit and cut-out. [10 marks]
(b) A customer buys a 10 A fuse to replace a 5 A fuse that keeps blowing. Explain why this is dangerous and what should be done. [5 marks]
(c) Explain three ways a seller can tell a genuine bulb from a fake one. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) battery: stores electrical energy, supplies starter and loads
2 marks: (a) alternator: generates electricity to charge battery and supply loads
2 marks: (a) ignition coil: steps up low voltage to high voltage for spark plugs
2 marks: (a) ECU: receives sensor signals and controls injection, ignition etc.
2 marks: (a) cut-out: disconnects dynamo from battery when output is low to prevent discharge
3 marks: (b) larger fuse allows excess current: wiring may overheat and cause fire
2 marks: (b) fault causing overload must be traced and repaired; fit correct rating
5 marks: (c) any three explained: packaging quality/brand marks, rating markings clear (W, V), holograms/serial numbers, weight/finish quality, source/price too low suspicious (5 marks for three well-explained, award 2+2+1)
questions.explanation: Battery stores energy; alternator generates; coil steps up voltage; ECU controls engine systems; cut-out prevents battery discharge through the dynamo. Oversized fuses let wires overheat: find the fault and fit the right fuse. Check markings, packaging, serials, finish and source.

questions.stem:
(a) What do the terms re-order level and re-order quantity mean to a storekeeper? [4 marks]
(b) A shop received 50 oil filters at ₦1,800 each on 1 March and 30 at ₦2,100 each on 10 March. On 15 March it sold 60 filters. Calculate the cost of filters sold and the value of closing stock using (i) FIFO, (ii) LIFO. [12 marks]
(c) Give two reasons why a dealer should neither overstock nor understock. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) re-order level: stock level at which a new order must be placed
2 marks: (a) re-order quantity: number of units ordered each time
3 marks: (b)(i) FIFO cost of sales = 50 x 1,800 + 10 x 2,100 = ₦111,000
3 marks: (b)(i) FIFO closing stock = 20 x 2,100 = ₦42,000
3 marks: (b)(ii) LIFO cost of sales = 30 x 2,100 + 30 x 1,800 = ₦117,000
3 marks: (b)(ii) LIFO closing stock = 20 x 1,800 = ₦36,000
4 marks: (c) any two: avoid running out and losing sales; avoid tying money in excess stock; reduce storage cost/damage (2 each)

questions.stem:
(a) Define sales and distinguish between cash and credit sales. [5 marks]
(b) Describe four methods of selling auto parts. [8 marks]
(c) Outline the procedure for making a sales call on a transport company. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) sales: exchange of goods for money/value
2 marks: (a) cash sale: payment made at time of purchase
2 marks: (a) credit sale: goods taken now, payment later at agreed date
8 marks: (b) any four described: personal selling, door-to-door, trade fair, open market, unit shop/retail, online (2 each)
1 mark: (c) prospecting/identify the company and decision maker
1 mark: (c) pre-approach: study its fleet and needs
1 mark: (c) book appointment
1 mark: (c) approach and introduce self/company
1 mark: (c) presentation/demonstration of parts and prices
1 mark: (c) handle objections
1 mark: (c) close the sale and follow up
questions.explanation: Sales exchange goods for value; cash is immediate, credit deferred. Methods include personal, door-to-door, trade fairs, open market and unit shops. Sales call: prospect, prepare, appoint, approach, present, handle objections, close and follow up.

questions.stem:
(a) Define advertising. [2 marks]
(b) Name four media of advertising suitable for an auto parts shop in a Nigerian town and state one advantage of each. [8 marks]
(c) Distinguish between informative and persuasive advertising. [4 marks]
(d) State three advantages of advertising to the shop. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) paid communication to inform or persuade buyers about goods/services
8 marks: (b) any four with advantage: radio (wide reach), newspaper (detail, record), handbills/posters (cheap, local), social media (cheap, targeted), signboard (permanent), TV (sight and sound) (1 medium + 1 advantage each)
2 marks: (c) informative: gives facts about products, prices, location
2 marks: (c) persuasive: urges/convinces customers to buy, stresses benefits
6 marks: (d) any three: increases sales, introduces new parts, builds brand/goodwill, informs about prices/location, meets competition (2 each)
questions.explanation: Advertising is paid communication to promote goods. Media: radio, newspapers, handbills, social media, signboards. Informative ads give facts; persuasive ads urge purchase. Advantages: more sales, awareness, goodwill, competitiveness.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of warranty. [3 marks]
(b) State three importance of a warranty to the buyer and two to the seller. [5 marks]
(c) Describe the procedure for claiming a warranty on a faulty starter motor. [6 marks]
(d) State three ways a customer can lose warranty rights. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) written promise by seller/manufacturer to repair or replace a product that fails within a stated period under normal use
3 marks: (b) buyer: confidence, protection against defects, free repair/replacement (1 each)
2 marks: (b) seller: attracts customers/goodwill, shows confidence in quality (1 each)
1 mark: (c) stop using part, check warranty period
1 mark: (c) gather receipt and warranty card
1 mark: (c) return part to seller/dealer within period
1 mark: (c) fill claim form/describe fault
1 mark: (c) seller inspects/tests or sends to manufacturer
1 mark: (c) repair, replacement or refund given
6 marks: (d) any three: expiry of period, wrong fitting/misuse, tampering or unauthorised repair, no receipt, accident damage, removing serial labels (2 each)
questions.explanation: A warranty is a promise to repair or replace within a period. Buyers gain protection; sellers gain goodwill. Claim with receipt and card, return part, have it tested, receive remedy. Rights are lost by expiry, misuse, tampering or lack of proof.
